posts.author: Satanicoaldo
posts.body:
So I just finished my first game, I used RPG maker 2000, and I noticed all the assets in my library end up in the file of the finished game.
This is an issue because I have collected a very extensive library of charactersets, facesets and tilesets and I didn't use ALL of them in the game.
So this situation made the game quite heavy, at least compared to what it could be or what i imagined it would be.
Is there anyway to make the final product files contain only the assets I use and not all assets I own?
Thank you very much for any help or clarification!

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
There is no native method or tool that can remove unused assets, but I have done this using another tool to import only the RTP assets that are actually being used, but it is not easy.
The best way is to never put files directly into the game folder, only use the manager.
Another thing is to never keep assets that you only imported for testing, they should be removed afterwards, always have a folder on your desktop where you will edit the assets before importing them, which will be the editable files, also never edit any assets that are already in the project folder.
I don't know if this tool would work with Rm2k 1.51(1.61) RTP, but I'll do some tests when I get home.

posts.author: Satanicoaldo
posts.body: Can you clue me in the tool's name?

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
RMTool - Download
The instructions below are at your own risk:
Close RPG Maker
For safety's sake, make a copy of your project folder.
In
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RPG Maker 2000
make a copy of the RTP folder
Copy all of your project folders to the original RTP folder
Delete the contents of the folders inside your project folder, but not the folders
Use
RMTool
as shown in the tutorial
Wait, read and do the import process
After finishing, which may take a while, close
RMTool
Delete the RTP folder and rename the "
Copy of RTP
" folder to RTP
The folder name will probably be "
Cópia de RTP
" if your operating system is PT or PT-BR.
Open
RPG Maker 2000
, load your project and see if everything is normal
Check the size of your project folder in Explorer
I repeat, the rich are on their own...
The interesting thing is that with this tool you can also find out where an event is using RTP assets so you can remove it instead of importing it, giving you the exact location, whether it is on a map or in some tab in the database.
Good lucky!
